Today's international headlines:
- What we know about the longest ground stop since 9/11: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack or a Microsoft outage.
- 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
- Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.
- Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage as it reports broad recovery: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
- Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
- Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
- Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague: Scott Bessent suggests Howard Lutnick’s commerce department failed to ban exports of Nvidia's chips to a firm thought to have links with China.
- The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
- German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad: German reforms mean foreign and domestic intelligence services will have greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage.
- Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
- Aide to fugitive Ukrainian ex-PM wounded in latest Moscow car bombing: Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was previously an adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov.
- Rosalía scoops historic third best album award at Latin Grammys: The Spanish singer is recognised for her fourth album Lux which was released last year to rave reviews.
